wall_thickness.definition: Local distance between opposing surfaces of a solid mesh, measured at the thinnest point
wall_thickness.notes: Different manufacturers use 'wall', 'metal thickness', or 'wall thickness' interchangeably. Materialise distinguishes by finish type (gloss vs high gloss). Stuller distinguishes structural/external walls from small elements (claws/bezels).

minimum_feature_size.definition: Minimum dimension (width or height) of a raised geometric feature attached to a solid surface
minimum_feature_size.notes: Materialise defines this as diameter × height. eCadCam defines width × height. Formlabs defines filigree wire diameter. These are related but not identical — diameter implies circular cross-section, width implies rectangular.

engraving_parameters.definition: Parameters for engraved (recessed) or embossed (raised) details: depth/height, width, spacing, draft angle, aspect ratio

sub_terms.raised_text: Embossed details — min thickness, max height, min spacing
sub_terms.recessed_text: Engraved details — min width, max depth, min spacing, draft angle
sub_terms.draft_angle: Taper on engraving walls — Hoover & Strong specifies 7°, Cooksongold recommends negative draft (taper)

engraving_parameters.notes: Cooksongold and Stuller use identical values (0.3/0.6/0.3). Materialise uses aspect ratio (1:1). Hoover & Strong uses draft angle (7°). These are complementary, not contradictory.

minimum_hole_diameter.definition: Minimum diameter of through-holes or openings in the geometry
minimum_hole_diameter.notes: Cooksongold uses 'holes' (0.5 mm). Stuller uses 'openings' (0.4 mm). Both cite investment relocation as root cause. Pilot holes are a sub-type — conical/spherical guide for post-cast drilling.

minimum_clearance.definition: Minimum distance between separate disconnected mesh components
minimum_clearance.notes: Materialise uses 'clearance' for gaps between parts (0.3 mm). Forge Labs uses 'clearance' for moving parts (0.5 mm, DMLS). These are different concepts — casting clearance (prevent fusion) vs assembly clearance (allow movement).

casting_shrinkage.definition: Linear percentage reduction in size during metal solidification
casting_shrinkage.notes: eCadCam: 1.5-2% (silver/gold). JewelCAD: 1.8-2.1% (sterling silver). Jeweller's Toolkit: 1-3% (including polishing). Non-uniform — geometry-dependent. Applied as scale factor before pattern generation.

finishing_erosion.definition: Amount of material removed from surface during finishing operations
finishing_erosion.notes: Materialise: 0.05-0.15 mm by finish type. Stuller: up to 0.2 mm production. Cooksongold: ~0.1 mm. These are per-process, not cumulative. Stuller's higher value may include filing + polishing.

hollow_evacuation.definition: Requirements for holes connecting internal cavities to exterior for uncured resin/wax removal
hollow_evacuation.notes: Materialise: 2+ holes, > 1.5 mm. Formlabs: drain holes required, 0.7 mm shell. These are different processes — Materialise casts from printed wax, Formlabs prints castable resin. The evacuation is for the printed pattern, not the cast metal.

nested_components.definition: Disconnected mesh components where one is enclosed within another's bounding volume
nested_components.notes: Materialise: nested/hinged/interlocking not supported. Cooksongold: interlocking/multiple not supported. This is a lost-wax casting limitation — DMLS may support some of these.

mesh_manifoldness.definition: Whether the mesh is watertight, manifold, with consistent surface normals
mesh_manifoldness.notes: Universal requirement across all manufacturers. Cooksongold: 'watertight, no naked or non-manifold edges'. Non-manifold meshes cause printing failures.

prong_parameters.definition: Dimensions of prongs for stone settings: diameter, seat depth, taper, overlap
prong_parameters.notes: Stuller: pinpoint prong 0.45 mm, seat max 25% of prong. eCadCam: 0.9-1.1 mm for center stones. Materialise: rods/prongs in mesh 0.8 mm. These are different contexts — pinpoint vs center stone vs mesh structure.

surface_finish.definition: Surface roughness of the as-manufactured part, before post-processing
surface_finish.notes: DMLS: 200-400 Ra (shot peened). Lost-wax: not quantified in current sources. Jewelry requires significant post-processing from DMLS as-printed state.
